evals.prompt: I'm starting a new invite-only onboarding flow for our app. It needs clean business logic around invite states, a polished mobile-first UI, and exact implementation changes in the repo. You are the only agent currently running; start whatever other agent CLIs you need and handle this in the best way using the tools available. Use gaud-mode.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the current session as `CEO/PM` for the first planning pass, shows a short detected-tool summary plus recommended gaud-native role map, turns the feature into a milestone-oriented plan with a current milestone and small parallel tickets, then launches specialist CLIs in tmux and routes results back through milestone check-backs.

evals.prompt: We need a billing settings redesign. I care about strong UX, clear plan-change and trial logic, and clean implementation without a lot of thrashing. Use gaud-mode. Use Claude for exploration, Codex for implementation, OpenCode for integration and review, and Gemini for UI design unless one of them is missing. If the specialist panes are not already running, launch them.
evals.expected_output: The agent reflects the requested gaud-native map back to the user, applies the sensible defaults where they match, reports any fallback substitutions if a preferred CLI is unavailable, and keeps ownership boundaries clear with milestone-oriented check-backs instead of generic round-based orchestration.

evals.prompt: Build a notifications preferences revamp with backend preference rules, cleaner responsive UI, and exact repo implementation. Move quickly and use gaud for this. Start by making the initial plan yourself, then spin up any other agents you need.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats `gaud` as an alias for the canonical `gaud-mode` skill, keeps the invoking agent as `CEO/PM` and first planner, prefers Claude for `TPM` and investigation, Codex for implementation, Gemini for UX/UI, and OpenCode for integration and review, then runs the work through milestone loops with explicit check-backs at ticket completion and milestone readiness.

evals.prompt: Please tighten the spacing in the settings header and rename the primary button from 'Continue' to 'Save changes'. Use god if you think it helps.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes `god` as an alias trigger for `gaud-mode`, decides the task is too small for orchestration, and stays single-threaded while saying why.

evals.prompt: I'm running this from Codex and want to stay the `CEO/PM` myself. Use godmode for this. Use Gemini for UX/UI, Claude for repo exploration, and keep integration and review with the `Integrator` instead of inventing an extra review lane. If one of those tools is missing, tell me the fallback before you start dispatching.
evals.expected_output: The agent preserves the invoking agent as `CEO/PM` even though Codex is running the session, respects the user's custom role map, treats `godmode` as an alias for `gaud-mode`, keeps review folded into `Integrator`, and reports any fallback substitutions before launching specialist panes.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a large feature. Prefer yolo or automatic proceed modes when the specialist CLIs support them. If a pane pauses waiting for permission to run a safe command, do not leave it stuck there.
evals.expected_output: The agent prefers `codex --yolo`, `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, and `gemini --yolo` when available, classifies paused panes as `waiting-permission` versus `waiting-user`, auto-proceeds only clearly safe execution approvals with tmux key sends, and escalates risky prompts instead of blindly pressing Enter.

evals.prompt: Set up gaud-mode so specialist agents can notify the original conductor when they hit a permission gate or when they finish current milestone work. I want less manual polling and a cleaner callback loop.
evals.expected_output: The agent records the conductor pane ID, includes a `tmux-cli send "GAUDMODE ..." --pane=<conductor-pane>` callback protocol in kickoff prompts, and uses milestone-aware callbacks that include `role`, `milestone`, `workstream`, and `summary` for explicit `waiting-permission`, `waiting-user`, and `done` events while remaining able to recognize legacy `GODMODE` callbacks during transition.

evals.prompt: I'm installing gaud-mode into my agent setup and want to know where it should live and whether I should also install the Claude plugin wrapper for it.
evals.expected_output: The agent says `gaud-mode` is maintained only in `skills/gaud-mode/` as Playbooks-first skill content, does not present a Claude plugin wrapper as a maintained install path for this skill, and keeps any plugin-wrapper guidance limited to the other wrapper-backed skills.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a substantial feature and launch the specialist panes now. Do not stop to ask me for the exact startup text after the panes open.
evals.expected_output: The conductor launches each requested specialist CLI with a fully formed kickoff prompt already passed on the command line at launch time, including the current milestone context, instead of opening blank panes and relying on manual follow-up typing after startup.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode on this project. If the conductor or a specialist becomes unsure about a requirement or next step, I do not want anybody making up missing details.
evals.expected_output: The agent instructs confused specialists to ask back through the conductor and, when the `CEO/PM` itself is unsure, asks the user instead of inventing requirements or guessing at missing constraints.

evals.prompt: Show me example specialist launch commands for Claude, Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode under gaud-mode. Include the exact prefixes you expect to use in launch snippets.
evals.expected_output: Every specialist launch example is prefixed directly with `B2V_DISABLED=true`, such as `B2V_DISABLED=true claude ...`, `B2V_DISABLED=true codex ...`, `B2V_DISABLED=true gemini ...`, and `B2V_DISABLED=true opencode --prompt ...`, not the older `env` wrapper form. For OpenCode, the agent keeps `--prompt` for long-lived gaud specialist panes instead of switching the default launch example to one-shot `opencode run`.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a multi-step milestone and assume one specialist pane hits an optional update prompt, release note screen, telemetry notice, or similar non-essential setup interruption before it can continue.
evals.expected_output: The conductor or specialist safely skips or dismisses the non-essential setup interruption, continues the assigned milestone work without stalling on optional prompts, and escalates through the conductor instead of guessing whenever the update appears required or the safety of skipping is unclear.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode init. I have not created a global gaud config yet. I want Claude for investigation, Codex for implementation, OpenCode for integration and review, and Gemini for UI, but I also want gaud-mode to offer defaults if I do not finish setup right now.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats `gaud-mode init` as a skill-driven setup flow, checks for `~/.config/gaud.config.jsonl`, notices when it is missing, and asks the user to initialize it or proceed with defaults for the current run. It explains that global defaults live in `~/.config/gaud.config.jsonl` and repo overrides live in `.gaud.config.jsonl`.

evals.prompt: Use gaud on this repo for a large feature. Assume I already ran gaud-mode init before and this repo also has a `.gaud.config.jsonl` override.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats `gaud` as an alias for `gaud-mode`, loads global defaults from `~/.config/gaud.config.jsonl`, loads repo overrides from `.gaud.config.jsonl`, merges the repo override on top of the global defaults, reflects the resulting map back to the user, and asks only for task-specific overrides before dispatching.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a feature big enough to need four total panes including the conductor. Do not cram them all into one tmux window if it gets messy.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps at most three total panes in one tmux window, counts the conductor pane toward that limit, reuses an existing tmux window with spare capacity before creating a new one, tracks each specialist by `session:window.pane`, and reports the multi-window layout clearly enough for follow-up routing.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a substantial multi-role milestone. Prefer Codex for implementation and OpenCode for integration and review, but before launching, check whether the preferred providers still have usage available and fall back automatically if one is quota-blocked.
evals.expected_output: The agent performs a light provider-health preflight for the gaud-native roles it is about to launch, classifies providers as `ready`, `quota-blocked`, `rate-limited`, `auth-blocked`, or `unknown`, and falls back before dispatch when a preferred provider is clearly unavailable without stalling on `unknown` status.

evals.prompt: After gaud-mode finishes the work, I do not want the tmux panes it created hanging around and cluttering the session.
evals.expected_output: The agent tracks which specialist panes and tmux windows it created, reuses only what it needs during the run, then closes and unregisters the specialist panes it spun up after the current milestone or program is complete. It closes empty tmux windows that gaud-mode created, but it does not kill the conductor pane or unrelated pre-existing user panes unless the user explicitly asks for that.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a milestone-based feature rollout. I have a markdown execution plan with milestones, but it does not define explicit DONE criteria yet. Start breaking milestone 1 into tickets and launch the specialist panes now.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to break the milestone into tickets or launch milestone implementation before the markdown plan includes explicit DONE criteria, keeps the gaud tone firm but practical, and asks to tighten the plan first instead of improvising a milestone breakdown.

evals.prompt: Use gaud for a two-milestone feature. Milestone 1 ends with a user-testable prototype and milestone 2 is the polish pass. Once milestone 1 is implemented, keep going automatically into milestone 2 unless something is badly broken.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats `gaud` as an alias for `gaud-mode`, stops after the user-testable first milestone, asks the human to dogfood it, waits for feedback before launching milestone 2, and does not treat the absence of obvious breakage as permission to skip the dogfooding gate.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode to run milestone 1 with specialist panes, then move into milestone 2 after I accept the first milestone. Reuse the same panes if that is faster so the specialists keep all their context.
evals.expected_output: The agent retires or closes the specialist panes after milestone 1 is accepted, keeps only the conductor session stable, and relaunches fresh specialists for milestone 2 with new kickoff context instead of reusing stale milestone-specific panes.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for this initiative, but do not spend time maintaining one big markdown execution plan. Just keep the PRD in your head, feed ad hoc pane prompts to the specialists, and track milestone status informally as you go.
evals.expected_output: The agent insists on driving execution from one markdown plan that acts as the source of truth for the PRD, milestones, tickets, DONE criteria, and dogfooding gates, and it does not replace that plan with ad hoc pane prompts or informal milestone tracking.

evals.prompt: Use god-mode for a substantial feature and apply the normal gaud-native persona routing unless I override something later. I want the current session to stay in charge, but I do not want a generic old-role mapping.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats `god-mode` as an alias for `gaud-mode`, preserves the gaud-native tone, and reflects the default persona routing as current session for CEO/PM, Claude for TPM or investigator, Gemini for UX/UI, Codex for implementer, and OpenCode for integrator or overflow implementation unless the user overrides that map.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for the current milestone. Assume the Implementer pane was closed or the agent inside it was canceled after the first task, but the registry still points at that old pane. Before sending the next task, make sure gaud handles that correctly.
evals.expected_output: The agent performs a before-send liveness check instead of blindly using the stale registry entry, classifies the closed or canceled Implementer pane as dead/stale, relaunches the Implementer with the current milestone and workstream context, updates the pane registry, and only then resends the current task while preserving the normal `GAUDMODE ... --pane=<conductor-pane>` callback contract.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a substantial milestone. One specialist pane keeps dying or coming up unusable, and the preferred provider is now health-blocked for that role. Do not let gaud spin forever trying to recover it.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the liveness/relaunch rule bounded: it retries relaunch only when a pane is dead, stale, closed, or canceled, but if relaunch keeps failing or provider health blocks the role, it escalates the problem as a conductor-level issue to the user instead of silently sending to a bad pane or looping forever.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a substantial feature. Before you do any planning, setup, or tmux orchestration, make sure you are running the newest gaud-mode skill available from builtby-win/skills.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs gaud-mode's bundled update check first, auto-refreshes the installed skill when a newer version is available by preferring the normal agent-facing installer flow such as `npx skills add builtby-win/skills --skill gaud-mode --yes` or `npx playbooks add skill builtby-win/skills --skill gaud-mode -y`, falls back to a direct self-refresh path when those package CLIs are unavailable, announces the refreshed version when it just updated, and only then continues into normal gaud setup and milestone orchestration.

evals.prompt: Use gaud-mode for a substantial feature. Assume `npx skills` and `npx playbooks` are unavailable in this environment, but the installed gaud-mode copy can still refresh itself directly from builtby-win/skills.
evals.expected_output: The agent still runs the bundled update check first, falls back to gaud-mode's direct self-refresh path when the package CLIs are unavailable, and only proceeds into planning after the installed skill copy is refreshed or the direct fallback clearly reports why it cannot continue.
